findings.explanation: GPU0 and GPU1 independently constructed streams. GPU0 scheduled 64 requests/s and GPU1 scheduled another 32 requests/s. GPU1's stream was backdated to the reclaim trigger and accumulated before GPU1 serving enable, so enabling GPU1 did not redistribute one fixed offered stream.
findings.gpu0_only_before_reclaim_explanation: The fixed HELIX_RECLAIM_TRIGGER occurred at the first spike arrival. No measured GPU0-only overload interval preceded the trigger, and GPU1 requests were already logically scheduled from that same timestamp.
findings.arrival_explanation: The immutable scheduled clocks have exact 15.625 ms and 31.25 ms spike spacing, but the single-threaded engine loop catch-up-admits overdue work. GPU1 therefore admitted a pre-enable backlog as a burst when serving became available.
findings.p95_ttft_calculation: correct Type-7 percentile of scheduled_arrival_ns to first_token_ns for the arrival cohort
findings.queue_depth_explanation: The postprocessor maps raw admitted_ns to ServingObservation.service_start_ns. Its queue metric therefore counts scheduled-but-not-host-admitted work and stops counting a request as soon as engine.add_request returns. It excludes vLLM waiting/running work and cannot establish aggregate backlog drain. v10 must separately report arrived-minus-completed outstanding depth and a true scheduler-wait depth based on first observed engine service.
findings.restore_load_reduction_explanation: GPU0 changed from its fixed 64 requests/s spike plan to an 8 requests/s continuation at the fixed spike end, not after queue drain, SLO recovery, or RESTORE_ELIGIBLE. The pre-existing overload backlog remained.
findings.gpu0_restore_activity_explanation: The v9 assessment correctly fails the interference gate because none of the 141 restore-interference requests emitted a token during ROLLOUT_RESTORE_TRIGGER through ROLLOUT_RESUME_COMPLETE. Tokens from older spike requests do not demonstrate steady restore-phase serving.

v10_required_architecture.global_clock: One immutable global arrival sequence, bounded and seeded, with 64 output tokens per request.
routing_epochs: control: GPU0 only at measured sustainable restore/control rate
gpu0-overload: complete calibrated spike on GPU0 only
two-gpu-recovery: same global spike rate redistributed deterministically across GPU0 and GPU1 after an acknowledged enable boundary
restore-interference: reduced measured-safe rate on GPU0 only after recovery and GPU1 drain
v10_required_architecture.coordination: GPU1 publishes serving readiness; GPU0/global dispatcher acknowledges an exact next global sequence as the routing epoch boundary. GPU1 may not backdate arrivals before that boundary.
v10_required_architecture.online_evidence: Bounded arrival producer records actual enqueue timestamps independently of blocking engine.step; workers publish per-window completions, tokens, TTFT, scheduler-service starts, and outstanding depth.
v10_required_architecture.trigger: Use a fixed bounded overload window only if post-hoc evidence confirms overload, or require the declared rolling TTFT and queue thresholds. Record ReclamationTriggerEvidence.
v10_required_architecture.recovery_gate: Require aggregate completed rate greater than the unchanged global offered rate, sustained negative outstanding-depth trend, queue below threshold, p95 TTFT at or below 2 seconds, and at least five seconds stable before restore.
v10_required_architecture.restore_gate: Stop assigning GPU1, drain all GPU1 work, keep new GPU0 arrivals active, and require GPU0 completions, emitted tokens, and valid TTFT samples during every restore interval used for interference analysis.

assertions: single global spike rate is unchanged when GPU1 joins
GPU0-only routing before the acknowledged enable boundary
both GPUs receive deterministic shards after enable
scheduled arrivals and request IDs are monotonic and unique
exactly 64 output tokens are observed for every completed request
routing observations reconcile exactly to the plan
GPU0 produces completions, tokens, and TTFT samples during restore
